event: Elsie asks if Cora slept at all; Cora says a Warden doesn't need much.
Elsie says that isn't an answer, and gives Cora back her coat, warm.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 42 → 43 (kindness: Elsie hands her coat back warm)

event: Tamsin wakes with Tilly's braid in her mouth and spits it out, and Tilly wakes indignant.
The shepherd comes up with a jug of milk for them and won't take a pip for it.
Elsie tells her the lights are harmless and the singing is a girl who means no harm.
Elsie says the passage has a wight in it, and the sheep are right to keep off the door.
The shepherd says she'll put a hurdle across it, and that's an end of it.
They start back east over the downs with the sun in their eyes.
Elsie walks and knits at once, the grey glove growing a thumb.
Cora asks, carefully, who the gloves are for.
Elsie says they're a surprise, and Cora looks straight ahead for a long while.
Tilly says she can't stop hearing the song; Tamsin says she can't either.
They come in by the west gate, and the gate clerk logs them in.
At the guild hall Cora hands in her report on the barrow at the clerk's desk.
The clerk reads it, stamps the notice done, and pays the reward out from the guild's box.

event: Tamsin counts it twice and grins; Tilly hugs Elsie off her feet.
Cora says she must write up the night for the guildmaster, and goes upstairs.
Elsie looks over at the corner of the board where the cast-off names go.
A woman sits alone at the corner table, and the tables round her stand empty.
She is slender, in a long dark green coat and black gloves, her black hair long and straight.
A man passing her table swerves wide, and his mug slops on the floor.
Elsie asks Tamsin who she is; Tamsin doesn't know, only that folk keep clear of that corner.
Tilly whispers that people swerve like that round bad luck.
Elsie says that sounds very lonely, and goes straight over with her tea.
She asks if the seat is free, and the woman says it's free, and that she shouldn't.
Elsie sits down, and the chair leg cracks, and she lands on the floor in her own tea.
The woman says: there. She's a Hexer, and bad luck lands on whoever sits near her.
Elsie laughs from the floor and says it's only tea, and takes the next chair along.
Tamsin and Tilly come over, and Tamsin sits down hard as if daring the chair.
Tilly sits too, and the strap of her vial belt snaps, and she catches every vial.
The woman watches them all as if they're mad, and says her name is Noor.
Elsie says hers is Elsie, and she's an Enthraller, so people keep their distance from her too.
Noor says she's heard; the whole hall has heard.
Elsie asks why Noor wears gloves; Noor says so she never touches anyone by mistake.
Elsie takes Noor's gloved hand in both of hers and says this isn't a mistake.

changes.note: Bond: Noor 0 → 2 (stand: Elsie takes her gloved hand, no mistake)

event: Noor goes very still, and doesn't pull it back.
Elsie's bootlace snaps, and she laughs again, and doesn't let go.
Noor says the last two parties she was in broke up around her, and everyone leaves.
Tamsin says three parties dropped her for worse than tea, and Elsie didn't.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 71 → 73 (stand: speaks for Elsie to Noor)

event: Tilly says the College threw her out for exploding things, and Elsie didn't mind that either.

changes.note: Bond: Tilly 53 → 55 (stand: speaks for Elsie to Noor; the scene's largest)

event: Noor says she's not asking to join anything; Elsie says she knows, she's asking Noor to lunch.
Noor says no, thank you, and takes her hand back slowly.
Elsie says then she'll come and sit here tomorrow, and the day after, until Noor says yes.
Noor says, dryly, that Elsie will run out of chairs.
Elsie asks Noor her favourite things, for her notebook; Noor stares at her.
Noor says, at last: rain, when the streets are empty, and black coffee.
Elsie writes it down, and draws a tiny raincloud beside Noor's name.
Noor sees the raincloud upside down, and her mouth twitches.
Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly go, and Elsie waves from the door; Noor lifts one gloved hand.
On the steps Tamsin says Elsie collects people like stray cats.
Elsie says she doesn't collect them, she just finds them, and they're all wonderful.
At the Tipsy Heron Elsie pays for soup and bread for the three of them.
Tilly drinks pear fizz and tells the barrow song to the soup, very badly.
Tamsin says she wrote to Nell about the shield-bearer, and dreads what Nell will say.
Elsie says Nell will say she's proud of her, and Tamsin says Nell has never once said that.
Elsie squeezes Tamsin's hand under the table, and Tamsin squeezes back and keeps it.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 73 → 75 (confidence: her dread of Nell, hand kept under the table)

event: Tilly goes home to read up on wights, and hugs Elsie goodbye.
Tamsin walks Elsie home along Willow Canal, past the blue door, which still has its card.
Elsie presses two fingers to it as she passes, and Tamsin presses hers there too.
At the Honeycomb Tamsin says she'll come by in the morning, and goes off to the wharf.
Elsie asks the baker if she may use the oven this evening, and the baker says yes.
In the attic Elsie sleeps the afternoon away with the window open.
She wakes, and waters the plants, and tells Moonpenny all about the singing.
She knits the grey glove's fingers until the thumb and all four are done.
She starts the second glove, humming the barrow song without knowing it.
Downstairs she buys honey from the baker for the cakes, and pays for it.
She bakes honey cakes in the big oven while the baker shows her the trick of the crust.
She sets a plate of them in the shop window, in case Amara comes by.
She wraps a few in paper for Noor tomorrow, and writes Noor on the paper.
The lamplighters' boats come by at dusk, and the honey cakes sit in the window untouched.
Elsie isn't sad about it; she says maybe means maybe, and eats one herself.
In the attic she writes her mother about the barrow, the singer, and the girl with gloves.
She writes that she thinks she has two new friends, only they don't know it yet.
From the round window she sees Cora on Thimble Canal, and waves the finished glove at her.
Cora stops, and looks at the glove a long time, and then puts her hand in her pocket.
Elsie goes to bed with the honey cake smell in her hair, and is asleep at once.
